context.purpose: Inspect an existing saved KiCad board, run KiCad's own design rule check, and export Excellon drill files, with each conclusion independently checked against the board geometry.
context.assumptions: A saved two-copper-layer .kicad_pcb in KiCad 8.0-10.0 format, with optional sibling .kicad_pro/.kicad_dru of the same name. Lengths are millimetres; KiCad board coordinates are y-down. kicad-cli runs isolated from global configuration and library tables on captured copies.
context.constraints: Board at most 4 MiB, 2000 tracks/arcs/vias and 2000 holes; only through vias from F.Cu to B.Cu; no oval/offset/backdrilled holes or footprint-owned Edge.Cuts. Drill export needs front-side drilled footprints. No board authoring, zone refill, schematic parity, Gerber/STEP/position outputs or drill maps.
context.inspection: Review board-summary.json: host counts, outline, minimum width/drill/clearance and the native statistics cross-check; for DRC the native findings by type, ignored checks, host predictions and the authored-maximum assessment; for drill export every hit matched by position, diameter and plating.
context.recovery: UNSUPPORTED_BOARD names the unsupported structure; edit the board in KiCad or choose a supported board. DRC_VIOLATIONS retains the native report and summary; fix the board or raise a maximum only with a recorded justification. VERIFICATION_FAILED means a native report disagreed with the host reader; retain the run and report it. Configure KiCad 10.0 kicad-cli for INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND/UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME.

workflow.scope: Verified board-summary, native DRC report and drill publications with digests; no downstream consumer is declared.

composition.scope: Shared document references, pure values and explicit finite visits; each visit captures its own board inputs.

lifecycle.timeout: One total deadline covers version, statistics, DRC and drill stages plus final independent verification; each stage receives the remaining budget and the shared supervisor stops the process tree.
lifecycle.cancellation: Owned process cancellation covers each native stage; cancellation is checked again before successful publication.
lifecycle.logs: Retain authored/effective plans, captured board/project copies and source digests, isolated native home, per-stage stdout/stderr/submissions, runtime identity, native statistics/DRC/drill outputs, summary and failed/success results.
lifecycle.verification: An independent dependency-free s-expression reader recomputes counts, outline, holes, track widths and gaps; native statistics must agree, DRC JSON is structurally validated against the observed runtime and its clearance/unconnected findings compared with host predictions where modelled; every Excellon hit is matched to a board hole within half a written digit. Retained inputs are re-hashed after every native stage.

losses: Global library tables, schematic, zone refill and 3D models are not used.
data.scope: Saved existing board read-only; captured copy is checked for mutation.

losses: Host predictions cover only straight-track/through-via clearance and simple pad connectivity; other DRC rules are native-only.
data.scope: Host facts, native cross-checks, DRC assessment and drill matching.

losses: Item UUIDs refer to the captured board copy.
data.scope: Native findings, unconnected items and ignored checks.

data.format: Excellon decimal, absolute origin, mm or inch
losses: No slots, drill maps, job file or Gerber layers; tool numbering is KiCad's.

inspection.scope: Read board-summary.json, the native DRC report and Excellon files as text with their cross-check results.
inspection.limits: No board rendering, layer viewer or interactive marker navigation.

authoring.reuse: Edit the board path, DRC maximums or drill options in the JSON document; plan, run and verify a fresh directory. Unchanged verified inputs are reused.

workflow.scope: Verified board summaries, native DRC reports and drill files are workflow publications with digests; no downstream adaptor consumes them yet and acceptedArtifacts is empty.

native-inspection.scope: Board inspection is a batch operation (inspectBoard); there is no live native inspection hook.

composition.scope: Shared document references, pure values and explicit finite analytic visits; each visit captures and checks its own board inputs.

mpi.scope: kicad-cli runs serially in one process; MPI is not applicable.

reusable-inputs.scope: Board and sibling .kicad_pro/.kicad_dru digests bind reuse; DRC_VIOLATIONS and failed checks are never reused as success.

source-authoring.scope: Shared durable document source editing and undo for the small JSON request; the board itself is not authored.

property-authoring.scope: Shared pointer edits for board path, maximum DRC counts, drill units and plating split.

live-editing.scope: No live KiCad session; board editing stays in KiCad.

native-save.scope: The adaptor never saves, upgrades or refills the board; captured copies are checked for mutation after each native stage.

conversion.scope: No format conversion operation; drill export is a fabrication output, not a board conversion.

cases.scope: Original 30 x 20 mm board: J1 (2 PTH, 1.0 mm), R1 (2 SMD), H1/H2 (3.2 mm NPTH), two 0.3 mm vias. Closest different-net tracks end 1.9 mm apart with 0.25 mm widths: 1.65 mm.
Every net is routed by construction and all gaps exceed the 0.2 mm Default clearance; library checks are ignored by the fixture project. Expect zero findings and confirmed host predictions.
Six round holes: four plated (two 1.0 mm pads, two 0.3 mm vias) and two 3.2 mm non-plated, in separate millimetre PTH/NPTH files.

Original 40 x 25 mm variant: J1 rotated 270 degrees with 3 PTH, two 0.8/0.4 mm vias for SIG and one for VCC, H1/H2 3.2 mm and H3 2.2 mm NPTH; one merged inch drill file. Closest gap is the VCC stub end to the 0.4 mm GND track: 1.9-0.15-0.2 = 1.55 mm.

completion.scope: New adaptor schemaxis.kicad/1: inspectBoard, designRuleCheck and drillExport, all fields, guidance, search cases, Studio starters, docs/kicad.md, examples, fixtures, host tests and KiCad 10.0.7 native acceptance.

notApplicable.mpi: kicad-cli runs serially in one process; MPI is not applicable.
